scope: Exodus 32–34, all 93 public verses. Prior revisions remain unchanged.

source.verse_hash_method: SHA-256 of the exact original XML verse substring, including written/read notes, not a normalized substitute.
source.public_versification_note: Public and Hebrew numbering align throughout Exodus 32–34.

delta_method: F0 retained wording; F1 lexical; F2 syntax/idiom; F3 consequential interpretive, textual, social, or versification choice. Editorial assessments are separate from similarity scores. Independent review has not occurred.

verses.rationale: Retains impatient demand, distancing this Moses, and plural divine designation supported by plural verb; no invented motive beyond stated delay.
verses.before: When the people saw that Moses delayed in coming down from the mountain, the people gathered around Aaron and said to him, “Rise, make gods for us who will go before us, for this Moses, the man who brought us up from the land of Egypt—we do not know what has happened to him.”
verses.after: When the people saw that Moses was taking a long time to come down the mountain, they gathered around Aaron and said, “Come, make us gods to go ahead of us. As for this Moses, the man who brought us up from Egypt, we do not know what has happened to him.”
verses.tsw_comparator: When the people saw that Moses delayed in coming down from the mountain, the people gathered around Aaron and said to him, “Rise, make gods for us who will go before us, for this Moses, the man who brought us up from the land of Egypt—we do not know what has happened to him.”

verses.rationale: Makes ear-worn jewelry natural while retaining all three gendered family groups and Aaron’s command.
verses.before: Aaron said to them, “Tear off the gold rings that are in the ears of your wives, your sons, and your daughters, and bring them to me.”
verses.after: Aaron answered, “Take off the gold earrings your wives, sons, and daughters are wearing, and bring them to me.”
verses.tsw_comparator: Aaron said to them, “Tear off the gold rings that are in the ears of your wives, your sons, and your daughters, and bring them to me.”

verses.rationale: Retains all-people action and actual possessors without rewriting compliance to match the prior family list.
verses.before: So all the people tore off the gold rings that were in their ears and brought them to Aaron.
verses.after: So all the people took off the gold earrings they were wearing and brought them to Aaron.
verses.tsw_comparator: So all the people tore off the gold rings that were in their ears and brought them to Aaron.

verses.rationale: Retains Aaron’s manufacture and collective acclamation; takes difficult tool expression as engraving and preserves plural declaration despite single calf.
verses.before: He took the gold from their hand, fashioned it with a tool, and made it into a cast calf. Then they said, “These are your gods, Israel, who brought you up from the land of Egypt!”
verses.after: He took the gold from their hands, shaped it with an engraving tool, and made it into a cast-metal calf. Then they said, “These are your gods, Israel, who brought you up from Egypt!”
verses.tsw_comparator: He took the gold from their hand, fashioned it with a tool, and made it into a cast calf. Then they said, “These are your gods, Israel, who brought you up from the land of Egypt!”

verses.rationale: Clarifies altar referent and retains festival explicitly dedicated to the LORD without harmonizing the preceding gods language.
verses.before: When Aaron saw this, he built an altar before it. Aaron proclaimed and said, “Tomorrow will be a festival to the LORD.”
verses.after: When Aaron saw this, he built an altar in front of the calf and announced, “Tomorrow will be a festival to the LORD.”
verses.tsw_comparator: When Aaron saw this, he built an altar before it. Aaron proclaimed and said, “Tomorrow shall be a festival to the LORD.”

verses.rationale: Preserves two offering types and meal-to-revelry sequence; does not add specific sexual acts to broad play verb.
verses.before: They rose early the next day and offered burnt offerings and brought offerings of well-being. The people sat down to eat and drink and rose up to revel.
verses.after: Early the next morning they offered burnt offerings and brought peace offerings. The people sat down to eat and drink, then got up to revel.
verses.tsw_comparator: They rose early the next day and offered burnt offerings and brought offerings of well-being. The people sat down to eat and drink and rose up to revel.

verses.rationale: Retains forceful descent command and divine attribution your people/you brought up, needed for Moses’ reversal in verse 11.
verses.before: Then the LORD spoke to Moses, “Go, get down, for your people whom you brought up from the land of Egypt have corrupted themselves.
verses.after: The LORD told Moses, “Go down! Your people, whom you brought up from Egypt, have acted corruptly.
verses.tsw_comparator: Then the LORD spoke to Moses, “Go, get down, for your people whom you brought up from the land of Egypt have corrupted themselves.

verses.rationale: Retains rapid departure, three calf actions, and exact repeated acclamation; no substitution of abstract idolatry for concrete acts.
verses.before: They have quickly turned aside from the way that I commanded them. They have made for themselves a cast calf, bowed down to it, sacrificed to it, and said, ‘These are your gods, Israel, who brought you up from the land of Egypt!’”
verses.after: They have quickly turned away from the way I commanded them to follow. They have made themselves a cast-metal calf, bowed down to it, and sacrificed to it, saying, ‘These are your gods, Israel, who brought you up from Egypt!’”
verses.tsw_comparator: They have quickly turned aside from the way that I commanded them. They have made for themselves a cast calf, bowed down to it, sacrificed to it, and said, ‘These are your gods, Israel, who brought you up from the land of Egypt!’”

verses.rationale: Keeps separate divine speech opening and embodied stubbornness image in short clauses.
verses.before: The LORD said to Moses, “I have seen this people, and look, it is a stiff-necked people.
verses.after: The LORD said to Moses, “I have seen these people. They are stiff-necked.
verses.tsw_comparator: The LORD said to Moses, “I have seen this people, and look, it is a stiff-necked people.

verses.rationale: Keeps requested nonintervention, destructive anger, and alternative nation promised to Moses without softening judgment.
verses.before: Now therefore leave me alone, so that my anger may burn against them and I may consume them. Then I will make a great nation from you.”
verses.after: Now leave me alone, so my anger may burn against them and I may consume them. Then I will make you into a great nation.”
verses.tsw_comparator: Now therefore leave me alone, so that my anger may burn against them and I may consume them. Then I will make a great nation from you.”

verses.rationale: Makes entreaty natural while preserving your people/you brought out reversal and strong-hand image.
verses.before: Yet Moses pleaded before the LORD his God and said, “Why, O LORD, should your anger burn against your people whom you brought out from the land of Egypt with great power and a strong hand?
verses.after: But Moses pleaded with the LORD his God: “LORD, why should your anger burn against your people, whom you brought out of Egypt with great power and a strong hand?
verses.tsw_comparator: But Moses pleaded before the LORD his God and said, “Why, O LORD, should your anger burn against your people whom you brought out from the land of Egypt with great power and a strong hand?

verses.rationale: Distinguishes Egyptians’ attributed evil intent from threatened disaster while retaining lethal content and explicit appeal to relent.
verses.before: Why should the Egyptians say, ‘For evil he brought them out, to kill them in the mountains and consume them from the face of the ground’? Turn from your burning anger and relent concerning this disaster against your people.
verses.after: Why should the Egyptians say, ‘He brought them out with evil intent, to kill them in the mountains and wipe them off the face of the ground’? Turn from your burning anger. Relent from bringing this disaster on your people.
verses.tsw_comparator: Why should the Egyptians say, ‘For evil he brought them out, to kill them in the mountains and consume them from the face of the ground’? Turn from your burning anger and relent concerning this disaster against your people.

verses.rationale: Keeps Israel rather than changing name to Jacob, divine self-oath, repeated offspring, stars and enduring land inheritance.
verses.before: Remember Abraham, Isaac, and Israel, your servants, to whom you swore by yourself and said to them, ‘I will multiply your offspring like the stars of the heavens, and all this land that I have spoken of I will give to your offspring, and they will inherit it forever.’”
verses.after: Remember your servants Abraham, Isaac, and Israel. You swore to them by your own self and said, ‘I will make your offspring as numerous as the stars in the sky. All this land I promised I will give to your offspring, and they will inherit it forever.’”
verses.tsw_comparator: Remember Abraham, Isaac, and Israel, your servants, to whom you swore by yourself and said to them, ‘I will multiply your offspring like the stars of the heavens, and all this land that I have spoken of I will give to your offspring, and they will inherit it forever.’”

verses.rationale: Retains narrative assertion of relenting without doctrinal paraphrase and keeps his people after the speech exchange.
verses.before: Then the LORD relented concerning the disaster that he had spoken of doing to his people.
verses.after: So the LORD relented from the disaster he had said he would bring on his people.
verses.tsw_comparator: Then the LORD relented concerning the disaster that he had spoken of doing to his people.

verses.rationale: Carries testimony term forward and preserves emphatic writing on both surfaces without invented inscription layout.
verses.before: Moses turned and went down from the mountain with the two tablets of the testimony in his hand, tablets written on both sides; on this side and on that side they were written.
verses.after: Moses turned and went down the mountain, carrying the two tablets of the testimony in his hand. They were written on both sides, front and back.
verses.tsw_comparator: Moses turned and went down from the mountain with the two tablets of the testimony in his hand, tablets written on both sides; on this side and on that side they were written.

verses.rationale: Maintains emphatic double divine authorship and engraving distinct from Moses’ later stone cutting.
verses.before: The tablets were the work of God, and the writing was the writing of God, engraved on the tablets.
verses.after: The tablets were God’s work, and the writing engraved on them was God’s writing.
verses.tsw_comparator: The tablets were the work of God, and the writing was the writing of God, engraved on the tablets.

verses.rationale: Keeps Joshua as speaker and his interpretation of sound rather than asserting an actual battle.
verses.before: Joshua heard the sound of the people as they shouted, and he said to Moses, “There is a sound of battle in the camp.”
verses.after: Joshua heard the people shouting and said to Moses, “There is the sound of battle in the camp!”
verses.tsw_comparator: Joshua heard the sound of the people as they shouted, and he said to Moses, “There is a sound of battle in the camp.”

verses.rationale: Preserves three-part sound contrast as lineated speech within verse paragraph and identifies Moses from dialogue context.
verses.before: Yet Moses said: “It is not the sound of a shout of victory, and not the sound of a cry of defeat; the sound of singing I hear.”
verses.after: Moses answered, “It is not the sound of victory, nor the sound of defeat; it is the sound of singing I hear.”
verses.tsw_comparator: But Moses said: “It is not the sound of a shout of victory, and not the sound of a cry of defeat; the sound of singing I hear.”

verses.rationale: Preserves sight-to-anger sequence, dancing, both hands reading, and violent shattering at mountain base; exact written/read record retained.
verses.before: As soon as he came near the camp and saw the calf and the dancing, Moses’ anger burned. He threw the tablets from his hands and shattered them at the foot of the mountain.
verses.after: As Moses approached the camp and saw the calf and the dancing, his anger burned. He threw the tablets from his hands and shattered them at the foot of the mountain.
verses.tsw_comparator: As soon as he came near the camp and saw the calf and the dancing, Moses’ anger burned. He threw the tablets from his hands and shattered them at the foot of the mountain.

verses.rationale: Retains every destructive and bodily action in order without inventing calf construction or reducing forced drinking to metaphor.
verses.before: He took the calf they had made, burned it with fire, ground it until it was fine, scattered it upon the water, and made the children of Israel drink it.
verses.after: He took the calf they had made, burned it in the fire, ground it to powder, scattered it over the water, and made the Israelites drink it.
verses.tsw_comparator: He took the calf they had made, burned it with fire, ground it until it was fine, scattered it upon the water, and made the children of Israel drink it.

verses.rationale: Keeps accusatory question and Aaron’s responsibility rather than assigning all blame to people.
verses.before: Moses said to Aaron, “What did this people do to you, that you brought such great sin upon them?”
verses.after: Moses said to Aaron, “What did these people do to you, that you brought such a great sin on them?”
verses.tsw_comparator: Moses said to Aaron, “What did this people do to you, that you brought such great sin upon them?”

verses.rationale: Preserves deferential human title and Aaron’s blame-shifting characterization as his speech.
verses.before: Aaron said, “Do not let the anger of my lord burn. You yourself know the people, that they are set on evil.
verses.after: Aaron replied, “Do not let your anger burn, my lord. You know these people and how bent they are on evil.
verses.tsw_comparator: Aaron said, “Do not let the anger of my lord burn. You yourself know the people, that they are set on evil.

verses.rationale: Retains repeated report closely matching verse 1, including distancing Moses and plural gods.
verses.before: They said to me, ‘Make gods for us who will go before us, for this Moses, the man who brought us up from the land of Egypt—we do not know what has happened to him.’
verses.after: They said to me, ‘Make us gods to go ahead of us. As for this Moses, the man who brought us up from Egypt, we do not know what has happened to him.’
verses.tsw_comparator: They said to me, ‘Make gods for us who will go before us, for this Moses, the man who brought us up from the land of Egypt—we do not know what has happened to him.’

verses.rationale: Preserves Aaron’s implausible account as reported speech, retaining its contrast with his deliberate craftsmanship in verse 4.
verses.before: So I said to them, ‘Whoever has gold, tear it off.’ They gave it to me, and I threw it into the fire, and out came this calf.”
verses.after: So I told them, ‘Whoever has gold, take it off.’ They gave it to me, I threw it into the fire, and out came this calf!”
verses.tsw_comparator: So I said to them, ‘Whoever has gold, tear it off.’ They gave it to me, and I threw it into the fire, and out came this calf.”

verses.rationale: Takes unrestrained sense of para rather than inserting nakedness; retains Aaron’s agency and hostile outsiders’ scorn.
verses.before: Moses saw that the people had broken loose, for Aaron had let them break loose, to become a derision among their enemies.
verses.after: Moses saw that the people were out of control. Aaron had let them loose, making them an object of scorn to their enemies.
verses.tsw_comparator: Moses saw that the people had broken loose, for Aaron had let them break loose, to become a derision among their enemies.

verses.rationale: Keeps allegiance summons and all sons of Levi as identifiable group without adding individual motives.
verses.before: Then Moses stood in the gate of the camp and said, “Whoever is for the LORD, come to me!” And all the sons of Levi gathered to him.
verses.after: Moses stood at the entrance to the camp and called, “Whoever is for the LORD, come to me!” All the Levites gathered around him.
verses.tsw_comparator: Then Moses stood in the gate of the camp and said, “Whoever is for the LORD, come to me!” And all the sons of Levi gathered to him.

verses.rationale: Retains Moses’ attribution to the LORD, sword command, traversal and lethal commands against close relationships without euphemism.
verses.before: He said to them, “Thus says the LORD, the God of Israel: Each man put his sword on his thigh. Pass back and forth from gate to gate throughout the camp, and each kill his brother, his companion, and his neighbor.”
verses.after: He told them, “This is what the LORD, the God of Israel, says: ‘Each of you, strap your sword to your side. Go back and forth through the camp, from entrance to entrance, and each of you kill his brother, his friend, and his neighbor.’”
verses.tsw_comparator: He said to them, “Thus says the LORD, the God of Israel: Each man put his sword on his thigh. Pass back and forth from gate to gate throughout the camp, and each kill his brother, his companion, and his neighbor.”

verses.rationale: Preserves approximate count, male victims, Levites’ action, and narrator’s fell image without reducing deaths to generic casualties.
verses.before: The sons of Levi did according to the word of Moses, and about three thousand men from the people fell that day.
verses.after: The Levites did as Moses said, and about three thousand men from the people fell that day.
verses.tsw_comparator: The sons of Levi did according to the word of Moses, and about three thousand men from the people fell that day.

verses.rationale: Renders fill-hands consecration idiom with imperative force; retains compressed kinship cost and blessing without claiming every Levite killed his own son.
verses.before: Moses said, “Fill your hands today for the LORD, for each was against his son and against his brother, so that he may give you a blessing today.”
verses.after: Moses said, “Consecrate yourselves to the LORD today, each at the cost of his son and his brother, so that he may give you a blessing today.”
verses.tsw_comparator: Moses said, “Fill your hands today for the LORD, for each was against his son and against his brother, so that he may give you a blessing today.”

verses.rationale: Retains great-sin repetition and perhaps uncertainty; preserves atonement term rather than promising certain forgiveness.
verses.before: The next day Moses said to the people, “You have sinned a great sin. And now I will go up to the LORD; perhaps I can make atonement for your sin.”
verses.after: The next day Moses told the people, “You have committed a great sin. Now I will go up to the LORD. Perhaps I can make atonement for your sin.”
verses.tsw_comparator: The next day Moses said to the people, “You have sinned a great sin. And now I will go up to the LORD; perhaps I can make atonement for your sin.”

verses.rationale: Preserves emotional plea, confession of collective sin, and gold-gods designation despite single-image narrative.
verses.before: Moses returned to the LORD and said, “Please! This people has sinned a great sin and made gods of gold for themselves.
verses.after: Moses returned to the LORD and said, “Oh, these people have committed a great sin! They have made themselves gods of gold.
verses.tsw_comparator: Moses returned to the LORD and said, “Please! This people has sinned a great sin and made gods of gold for themselves.

verses.rationale: Leaves first conditional plea unfinished as in Hebrew and retains Moses’ request for personal erasure without identifying an unstated book of life.
verses.before: And now, if you will forgive their sin—but if not, please wipe me out from your book that you have written.”
verses.after: Now, if you will forgive their sin— But if not, please erase me from the book you have written.”
verses.tsw_comparator: And now, if you will forgive their sin—but if not, please wipe me out from your book that you have written.”

verses.rationale: Preserves answer’s individual accountability and repeated book/erase language without adding afterlife explanation.
verses.before: The LORD said to Moses, “Whoever has sinned against me, I will wipe out from my book.
verses.after: The LORD replied to Moses, “Whoever has sinned against me, I will erase from my book.
verses.tsw_comparator: The LORD said to Moses, “Whoever has sinned against me, I will wipe out from my book.

verses.rationale: Keeps guidance promise alongside deferred reckoning and repeats visitation idiom as call to account rather than erasing accountability.
verses.before: And now go, lead the people to the place of which I spoke to you. Look, my messenger will go before you. But on the day I attend, I will attend to them for their sin.”
verses.after: Now go and lead the people to the place I told you about. My angel will go ahead of you. But when the day comes for me to call them to account, I will call them to account for their sin.”
verses.tsw_comparator: And now go, lead the people to the place of which I spoke to you. Look, my messenger will go before you. But on the day I attend, I will attend to them for their sin.”

verses.rationale: Keeps plague and deliberately repeated shared responsibility of people and Aaron instead of harmonizing one away.
verses.before: Then the LORD struck the people because they had made the calf, the one Aaron had made.
verses.after: The LORD struck the people with a plague because they had made the calf—the calf Aaron made.
verses.tsw_comparator: Then the LORD struck the people because they had made the calf, the one Aaron had made.

verses.rationale: Retains ascent, Moses-attributed deliverance, three patriarch names, and sworn offspring promise in clear nested sentence.
verses.before: And the LORD said to Moses, “Go up from here, you and the people whom you brought up from the land of Egypt, to the land that I swore to Abraham, to Isaac, and to Jacob, saying, ‘To your offspring I will give it.’”
verses.after: The LORD told Moses, “Leave this place and go up, you and the people you brought up from Egypt, to the land I swore to Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob to give to their offspring.
verses.tsw_comparator: And the LORD said to Moses, “Go up from here, you and the people whom you brought up from the land of Egypt, to the land that I swore to Abraham, to Isaac, and to Jacob, saying, ‘To your offspring I will give it.’”

verses.rationale: Preserves angel promise, divine displacement agency, and all six peoples in source order.
verses.before: “And I will send an angel before you, and I will drive out the Canaanite, the Amorite, the Hittite, the Perizzite, the Hivite, and the Jebusite.
verses.after: I will send an angel ahead of you and drive out the Canaanites, Amorites, Hittites, Perizzites, Hivites, and Jebusites.
verses.tsw_comparator: “And I will send an angel before you, and I will drive out the Canaanite, the Amorite, the Hittite, the Perizzite, the Hivite, and the Jebusite.

verses.rationale: Supplies contextual go for dependent land phrase while retaining bodily abundance, refusal of presence, stubbornness and potential destruction.
verses.before: Go to a land flowing with milk and honey. For I will not go up in your midst, because you are a stiff-necked people, lest I consume you on the way.”
verses.after: Go to a land flowing with milk and honey. But I will not go up among you, because you are a stiff-necked people and I might consume you on the way.”
verses.tsw_comparator: Go to a land flowing with milk and honey. For I will not go up in your midst, because you are a stiff-necked people, lest I consume you on the way.”

verses.rationale: Connects bad news to mourning and universal lack of adornment without inventing permanent ban.
verses.before: When the people heard this bad word, they mourned, and no one put on his adornment.
verses.after: When the people heard these grievous words, they mourned, and no one put on any ornaments.
verses.tsw_comparator: When the people heard this bad word, they mourned, and no one put on his adornment.

verses.rationale: Reads speech as explanation of preceding response; preserves conditional instantaneous danger and undecided next action.
verses.before: And the LORD said to Moses, “Say to the children of Israel, ‘You are a stiff-necked people. If I went up in your midst for one moment, I would consume you. Now take your adornment down from upon you, and I will know what I will do to you.’”
verses.after: The LORD had told Moses, “Say to the Israelites, ‘You are a stiff-necked people. If I went among you for even a moment, I would consume you. Now take off your ornaments, and I will decide what to do with you.’”
verses.tsw_comparator: And the LORD said to Moses, “Say to the children of Israel, ‘You are a stiff-necked people. If I went up in your midst for one moment, I would consume you. Now take your adornment down from upon you, and I will know what I will do to you.’”

verses.rationale: Takes from Horeb as the starting point for removal of adornment; preserves Horeb name rather than harmonizing to Sinai.
verses.before: So the children of Israel stripped themselves of their adornments from Mount Horeb.
verses.after: So the Israelites stripped off their ornaments from Mount Horeb onward.
verses.tsw_comparator: So the children of Israel stripped themselves of their adornments from Mount Horeb.

verses.rationale: Preserves habitual description, repeated outside location and access for anyone seeking; does not silently identify tent with unbuilt tabernacle.
verses.before: Now Moses would take the tent and pitch it for himself outside the camp, far from the camp; and he called it the Tent of Meeting. And everyone seeking the LORD would go out to the Tent of Meeting, which was outside the camp.
verses.after: Moses used to take the tent and pitch it outside the camp, far away from the camp. He called it the tent of meeting. Anyone seeking the LORD would go out to the tent of meeting outside the camp.
verses.tsw_comparator: Now Moses would take the tent and pitch it for himself outside the camp, far from the camp; and he called it the Tent of Meeting. And everyone seeking the LORD would go out to the Tent of Meeting, which was outside the camp.

verses.rationale: Clarifies individual tents versus meeting tent while retaining habitual collective standing and watching until entry.
verses.before: And whenever Moses went out to the tent, all the people would rise, and each would stand at the entrance of his tent and watch Moses until he entered the tent.
verses.after: Whenever Moses went out to the tent, all the people would rise and stand at the entrances to their own tents, watching Moses until he entered the tent.
verses.tsw_comparator: And whenever Moses went out to the tent, all the people would rise, and each would stand at the entrance of his tent and watch Moses until he entered the tent.

verses.rationale: Clarifies divine speaker from verse 11 rather than treating cloud as a separate speaking agent; retains cloud position and repeated pattern.
verses.before: And whenever Moses entered the tent, the pillar of cloud would come down and stand at the entrance of the tent, and he would speak with Moses.
verses.after: When Moses entered the tent, the pillar of cloud would come down and stand at its entrance, and the LORD would speak with Moses.
verses.tsw_comparator: And whenever Moses entered the tent, the pillar of cloud would come down and stand at the entrance of the tent, and he would speak with Moses.

verses.rationale: Retains universal observation and individual worship locations; source annotation remains fully bound.
verses.before: And all the people saw the pillar of cloud standing at the entrance of the tent; and all the people would rise and bow down, each at the entrance of his tent.
verses.after: When all the people saw the pillar of cloud standing at the tent’s entrance, they would rise and bow down, each at the entrance to their own tent.
verses.tsw_comparator: And all the people saw the pillar of cloud standing at the entrance of the tent; and all the people would rise and bow down, each at the entrance of his tent.

verses.rationale: Preserves face-to-face speech image alongside later no-face-vision claim, names Joshua and father, and retains young attendant’s continuing presence.
verses.before: And the LORD would speak with Moses face to face, as a man speaks with his companion. Then he would return to the camp, but his attendant Joshua son of Nun, a young man, would not depart from inside the tent.
verses.after: The LORD would speak to Moses face to face, as one person speaks to a friend. Then Moses would return to the camp, but his young assistant Joshua son of Nun would stay inside the tent.
verses.tsw_comparator: And the LORD would speak with Moses face to face, as a man speaks with his companion. Then he would return to the camp, but his attendant Joshua son of Nun, a young man, would not depart from inside the tent.

verses.rationale: Makes complaint and cited assurances followable while keeping know-by-name and favor-in-eyes images.
verses.before: Moses said to the LORD, “See, you say to me, ‘Bring up this people,’ but you have not revealed to me whom you will send with me. Yet you have said, ‘I know you by name, and you have also found favor in my sight.’
verses.after: Moses said to the LORD, “Look, you tell me, ‘Bring these people up,’ but you have not told me whom you will send with me. Yet you have said, ‘I know you by name, and you have found favor in my eyes.’
verses.tsw_comparator: Moses said to the LORD, “See, you say to me, ‘Bring up this people,’ but you have not made known to me whom you will send with me. Yet you have said, ‘I know you by name, and you have also found favor in my sight.’

verses.rationale: Retains knowing ways/knowing God/favor chain and Moses’ renewed appeal to your people.
verses.before: Now therefore, if I have found favor in your sight, show me now your ways, that I may know you, in order to find favor in your sight. Consider too that this nation is your people.”
verses.after: Now, if I have found favor in your eyes, please make your ways known to me, so I may know you and continue to find favor in your eyes. Consider too that this nation is your people.”
verses.tsw_comparator: Now therefore, if I have found favor in your sight, show me now your ways, that I may know you, in order to find favor in your sight. Consider too that this nation is your people.”

verses.rationale: Keeps face idiom as presence and singular rest recipient without inserting with all of you before Moses’ plural request.
verses.before: And he said, “My presence will go, and I will give you rest.”
verses.after: He answered, “My presence will go, and I will give you rest.”
verses.tsw_comparator: And he said, “My presence will go, and I will give you rest.”

verses.rationale: Preserves explicit group us in response to singular you and dependence of departure on presence.
verses.before: And he said to him, “If your presence does not go, do not bring us up from here.
verses.after: Moses replied, “If your presence does not go, do not bring us up from here.
verses.tsw_comparator: And he said to him, “If your presence does not go, do not bring us up from here.

verses.rationale: Retains repeated I and your people, presence as distinguishing criterion, and ground image without asserting ethnic superiority.
verses.before: For how will it be known that I have found favor in your sight, I and your people? Is it not in your going with us, so that we are set apart, I and your people, from all the people who are on the face of the earth?”
verses.after: How else will anyone know that I and your people have found favor in your eyes? Only by your going with us will I and your people be set apart from every other people on the face of the ground.”
verses.tsw_comparator: For how shall it be known that I have found favor in your sight, I and your people? Is it not in your going with us, so that we are set apart, I and your people, from all the people who are on the face of the earth?”

verses.rationale: Keeps response grounded in favor and personal knowing, mirroring assurances cited in verse 12.
verses.before: And the LORD said to Moses, “This very thing that you have spoken I will do, for you have found favor in my sight, and I know you by name.”
verses.after: The LORD told Moses, “I will do this too, just as you have asked, because you have found favor in my eyes and I know you by name.”
verses.tsw_comparator: And the LORD said to Moses, “This very thing that you have spoken I will do, for you have found favor in my sight, and I know you by name.”

verses.rationale: Clarifies requester and preserves brief direct plea without expanded interpretation of glory.
verses.before: Moses said, “Please show me your glory.”
verses.after: Moses said, “Please show me your glory.”
verses.tsw_comparator: Moses said, “Please show me your glory.”

verses.rationale: Retains all goodness, divine name proclamation and two deliberate repeated freedom-of-grace clauses without doctrinal elaboration.
verses.before: And he said, “I will cause all my goodness to pass before you and will proclaim the name of the LORD before you. And I will be gracious to whom I will be gracious, and will show compassion to whom I will show compassion.
verses.after: He answered, “I will make all my goodness pass before you and proclaim the name ‘the LORD’ in your presence. I will be gracious to whom I will be gracious, and I will show compassion to whom I will show compassion.”
verses.tsw_comparator: And he said, “I will cause all my goodness to pass before you and will proclaim the name of the LORD before you. And I will be gracious to whom I will be gracious, and will show compassion to whom I will show compassion.

verses.rationale: Preserves categorical human vision/life limit and face image without harmonizing away verse 11.
verses.before: But,” he said, “you cannot see my face, for man will not see me and live.”
verses.after: But he said, “You cannot see my face, for no human can see me and live.”
verses.tsw_comparator: But,” he said, “you cannot see my face, for man shall not see me and live.”

verses.rationale: Keeps spatial invitation and rock command in two natural clauses.
verses.before: And the LORD said, “Look, there is a place by me where you will stand on the rock,
verses.after: The LORD said, “Here is a place beside me. Stand on the rock.
verses.tsw_comparator: And the LORD said, “Behold, there is a place by me where you shall stand on the rock,

verses.rationale: Preserves glory, cleft, protective hand and until timing without replacing body imagery with abstract protection.
verses.before: and while my glory passes by I will put you in a cleft of the rock, and I will cover you with my hand until I have passed by.
verses.after: When my glory passes by, I will put you in a cleft in the rock and cover you with my hand until I have passed.
verses.tsw_comparator: and while my glory passes by I will put you in a cleft of the rock, and I will cover you with my hand until I have passed by.

verses.rationale: Retains contrasting hand/back/face imagery and prohibition rather than resolving into metaphorical aftereffects.
verses.before: Then I will take away my hand, and you will see my back, but my face will not be seen.”
verses.after: Then I will take away my hand, and you will see my back. But my face must not be seen.”
verses.tsw_comparator: Then I will take away my hand, and you shall see my back, but my face shall not be seen.”

verses.rationale: Distinguishes Moses cutting stones from God promising writing; preserves two, prior content and Moses’ responsibility for breakage.
verses.before: The LORD said to Moses, “Cut for yourself two tablets of stone like the first ones, and I will write upon the tablets the words that were on the first tablets, which you shattered.
verses.after: The LORD told Moses, “Cut two stone tablets like the first ones. I will write on them the words that were on the first tablets, which you shattered.
verses.tsw_comparator: The LORD said to Moses, “Cut for yourself two tablets of stone like the first ones, and I will write upon the tablets the words that were on the first tablets, which you shattered.

verses.rationale: Retains repeated morning, ascent, named mountain and appointed summit meeting.
verses.before: Be ready by morning and come up in the morning to Mount Sinai. Present yourself to me there on the top of the mountain.
verses.after: Be ready by morning. In the morning, come up Mount Sinai and stand before me there on the summit.
verses.tsw_comparator: Be ready by morning and come up in the morning to Mount Sinai. Present yourself to me there on the top of the mountain.

verses.rationale: Preserves comprehensive human exclusion and animal grazing boundary without restricting only summit.
verses.before: No one will come up with you, and no one will be seen anywhere on the mountain. Even the flocks and herds will not graze opposite that mountain.”
verses.after: No one is to come up with you, and no one is to be seen anywhere on the mountain. Even the flocks and herds must not graze in front of it.”
verses.tsw_comparator: No one shall come up with you, and no one shall be seen anywhere on the mountain. Even the flocks and herds shall not graze opposite that mountain.”

verses.rationale: Retains command-fulfillment sequence and repeated two stone tablets rather than compressing away their importance.
verses.before: So Moses cut two tablets of stone like the first ones. He rose early in the morning and went up Mount Sinai, as the LORD had commanded him, and took in his hand the two tablets of stone.
verses.after: Moses cut two stone tablets like the first ones. He rose early and went up Mount Sinai, as the LORD had commanded him, carrying the two stone tablets in his hand.
verses.tsw_comparator: So Moses cut two tablets of stone like the first ones. He rose early in the morning and went up Mount Sinai, as the LORD had commanded him, and took in his hand the two tablets of stone.

verses.rationale: Preserves pronoun for disputed proclamation subject, with note relating natural LORD reading and possible Moses invocation.
verses.before: The LORD descended in the cloud and stood with him there and proclaimed the name of the LORD.
verses.after: The LORD came down in the cloud and stood with him there. He proclaimed the name of the LORD.
verses.tsw_comparator: The LORD descended in the cloud and stood with him there and proclaimed the name of the LORD.

verses.rationale: Retains doubled name and ordered divine qualities, links hesed to faithful love in 20:6, and lineates proclamation within verse paragraph.
verses.before: The LORD passed before him and proclaimed: “The LORD, the LORD, a God compassionate and gracious, slow to anger, abundant in steadfast love and faithfulness,
verses.after: The LORD passed in front of him and proclaimed, “The LORD, the LORD, a God compassionate and gracious, slow to anger, abounding in faithful love and faithfulness,
verses.tsw_comparator: The LORD passed before him and proclaimed: “The LORD, the LORD, a God compassionate and gracious, slow to anger, abundant in steadfast love and faithfulness,

verses.rationale: Keeps unqualified thousands, three wrongdoing terms, emphatic nonacquittal and intergenerational divine reckoning; no added limiting clause or softened natural-consequences paraphrase.
verses.before: keeping steadfast love for thousands, forgiving guilt, transgression, and sin, yet by no means clearing the guilty, attending to the guilt of fathers upon children and children’s children, to the third and fourth generation.”
verses.after: keeping faithful love for thousands, forgiving guilt, rebellion, and sin, yet certainly not clearing the guilty, bringing the fathers’ guilt upon their children and grandchildren, to the third and fourth generations.”
verses.tsw_comparator: keeping steadfast love for thousands, forgiving guilt, transgression, and sin, yet by no means clearing the guilty, attending to the guilt of fathers upon children and children’s children, to the third and fourth generation.”

verses.rationale: Retains urgency and bodily prostration in response to proclamation.
verses.before: Moses hurried and bowed his head toward the ground and worshiped.
verses.after: Moses quickly bowed low to the ground and worshiped.
verses.tsw_comparator: Moses hurried and bowed his head toward the ground and worshiped.

verses.rationale: Takes ki concessively while noting causal alternative; preserves communal confession and inheritance request rather than separating Moses from people.
verses.before: He said, “If now I have found favor in your eyes, my Lord, please let my Lord go in our midst, though this is a stiff-necked people. Forgive our guilt and our sin, and take us as your inheritance.”
verses.after: He said, “My Lord, if I have found favor in your eyes, please go among us. Though this is a stiff-necked people, forgive our guilt and sin, and take us as your inheritance.”
verses.tsw_comparator: He said, “If now I have found favor in your eyes, my Lord, please let my Lord go in our midst, though this is a stiff-necked people. Forgive our guilt and our sin, and take us as your inheritance.”

verses.rationale: Keeps covenant making, created-wonders language, universal comparison and fear-inducing divine work without merely positive spectacle.
verses.before: He said, “Look, I am making a covenant. Before all your people I will do wonders that have not been created in all the earth or among any nation. All the people among whom you are will see the work of the LORD, for it is an awe-inspiring thing that I am doing with you.
verses.after: He answered, “Look, I am making a covenant. Before all your people I will do wonders unlike anything brought into being anywhere on earth or among any nation. All the people among whom you live will see the LORD’s work, for what I am doing with you is awe-inspiring.
verses.tsw_comparator: He said, “Look, I am making a covenant. Before all your people I will do wonders that have not been created in all the earth or among any nation. All the people among whom you are will see the work of the LORD, for it is an awe-inspiring thing that I am doing with you.

verses.rationale: Preserves command and divine displacement with six peoples in this verse’s order, differing from 33:2.
verses.before: Keep what I command you today. Look, I am driving out before you the Amorite, Canaanite, Hittite, Perizzite, Hivite, and Jebusite.
verses.after: Keep what I command you today. I am driving out before you the Amorites, Canaanites, Hittites, Perizzites, Hivites, and Jebusites.
verses.tsw_comparator: Keep what I command you today. Look, I am driving out before you the Amorite, Canaanite, Hittite, Perizzite, Hivite, and Jebusite.

verses.rationale: Retains covenant term for prohibited local pact and concrete snare image without broadening beyond stated inhabitants.
verses.before: Be careful not to make a covenant with the inhabitants of the land into which you are going, lest it become a snare in your midst.
verses.after: Be careful not to make a covenant with the inhabitants of the land you are entering, or it will become a snare among you.
verses.tsw_comparator: Be careful not to make a covenant with the inhabitants of the land into which you are going, lest it become a snare in your midst.

verses.rationale: Retains destructive commands and three different cult objects; keeps Asherah identity with concise vocabulary rather than generic trees.
verses.before: Rather, you will tear down their altars, shatter their pillars, and cut down their Asherah poles.
verses.after: Tear down their altars, shatter their sacred pillars, and cut down their Asherah poles.
verses.tsw_comparator: Rather, you shall tear down their altars, shatter their pillars, and cut down their Asherah poles.

verses.rationale: Preserves doubled divine jealousy and name claim without replacing with protective love or human insecurity commentary.
verses.before: For you will not bow down to another god, for the LORD, whose name is Jealous, is a jealous God.
verses.after: You must not bow down to another god, because the LORD, whose name is Jealous, is a jealous God.
verses.tsw_comparator: For you shall not bow down to another god, for the LORD, whose name is Jealous, is a jealous God.

verses.rationale: Retains sexual-infidelity metaphor and invitation-to-sacrifice sequence without asserting literal cult prostitution.
verses.before: Do not make a covenant with the inhabitants of the land, lest when they prostitute themselves after their gods and sacrifice to their gods, someone invite you and you eat from his sacrifice,
verses.after: Do not make a covenant with the land’s inhabitants. When they prostitute themselves to their gods and sacrifice to them, someone may invite you, and you may eat from his sacrifice.
verses.tsw_comparator: Do not make a covenant with the inhabitants of the land, lest when they prostitute themselves after their gods and sacrifice to their gods, someone invite you and you eat from his sacrifice,

verses.rationale: Preserves specific daughters/sons marriage direction and repeated prostitution metaphor as religious allegiance, not generic intermarriage ban.
verses.before: and you take some of their daughters for your sons, and their daughters prostitute themselves after their gods and cause your sons to prostitute themselves after their gods.
verses.after: You may take their daughters as wives for your sons, and when their daughters prostitute themselves to their gods, they will lead your sons to prostitute themselves to those gods too.
verses.tsw_comparator: and you take some of their daughters for your sons, and their daughters prostitute themselves after their gods and cause your sons to prostitute themselves after their gods.

verses.rationale: Keeps material specification and gods language directly recalling calf episode.
verses.before: You will not make for yourself cast gods.
verses.after: Do not make cast-metal gods for yourselves.
verses.tsw_comparator: You shall not make for yourself cast gods.

verses.rationale: Retains seven days, repeated Abib, appointment and exodus rationale with established festival name.
verses.before: “You will keep the Festival of Unleavened Bread. Seven days you will eat unleavened bread, as I commanded you, at the appointed time in the month of Abib, for in the month of Abib you came out from Egypt.
verses.after: Keep the Festival of Unleavened Bread. For seven days eat unleavened bread, as I commanded you, at the appointed time in the month of Abib, because it was in Abib that you came out of Egypt.
verses.tsw_comparator: “You shall keep the Festival of Unleavened Bread. Seven days you shall eat unleavened bread, as I commanded you, at the appointed time in the month of Abib, for in the month of Abib you came out from Egypt.

verses.rationale: Preserves opening-womb image and male specification of livestock with note acknowledging difficult compressed Hebrew form.
verses.before: Everything that first opens the womb is mine, including every male firstborn among your livestock, whether cattle or sheep.
verses.after: Every firstborn that opens the womb belongs to me, including every firstborn male among your cattle and flocks.
verses.tsw_comparator: Everything that first opens the womb is mine, including every male firstborn among your livestock, whether cattle or sheep.

verses.rationale: Preserves redemption, explicit animal harm, all firstborn sons, and appearance requirement; seh rendered sheep or goat consistent with its range.
verses.before: The firstborn donkey you will redeem with a lamb, but if you do not redeem it, you will break its neck. Every firstborn of your sons you will redeem. No one will appear before me empty-handed.
verses.after: Redeem a firstborn donkey with a sheep or goat. If you do not redeem it, break its neck. Redeem every firstborn son. No one is to appear before me empty-handed.
verses.tsw_comparator: The firstborn donkey you shall redeem with a lamb, but if you do not redeem it, you shall break its neck. Every firstborn of your sons you shall redeem. No one shall appear before me empty-handed.

verses.rationale: Retains repeated cessation and both agricultural peak-work exceptions without allowing seasonal exemption.
verses.before: Six days you will work, but on the seventh day you will cease. Even in plowing time and harvest you will cease.
verses.after: Work for six days, but stop on the seventh. Even during plowing and harvest, you must stop.
verses.tsw_comparator: Six days you shall work, but on the seventh day you shall cease. Even in plowing time and harvest you shall cease.

verses.rationale: Keeps both named festivals, wheat specificity and seasonal turn without equating to modern calendar date.
verses.before: You will keep the Festival of Weeks, the firstfruits of the wheat harvest, and the Festival of Ingathering at the turning of the year.
verses.after: Keep the Festival of Weeks with the firstfruits of the wheat harvest, and the Festival of Ingathering at the turn of the year.
verses.tsw_comparator: You shall keep the Festival of Weeks, the firstfruits of the wheat harvest, and the Festival of Ingathering at the turning of the year.

verses.rationale: Retains explicit male attendance, three times and layered divine titles, using the same Lord GOD convention as 23:17, without expanding participants to all genders.
verses.before: Three times in the year all your males will appear before the Lord GOD, the God of Israel.
verses.after: Three times a year all your males must appear before the Lord GOD, the God of Israel.
verses.tsw_comparator: Three times in the year all your males shall appear before the Lord GOD, the God of Israel.

verses.rationale: Preserves divine displacement and territorial expansion, coveting rather than only invasion, and repeated attendance count.
verses.before: For I will drive out nations before you and enlarge your territory, and no one will desire your land when you go up to appear before the LORD your God three times in the year.
verses.after: For I will dispossess nations before you and enlarge your territory. No one will covet your land when you go up three times a year to appear before the LORD your God.
verses.tsw_comparator: For I will drive out nations before you and enlarge your territory, and no one will desire your land when you go up to appear before the LORD your God three times in the year.

verses.rationale: Keeps blood/leaven prohibition and explicitly Passover leftover rule without broadening to all offerings.
verses.before: You will not offer the blood of my sacrifice with anything leavened, and the sacrifice of the Passover festival will not remain until morning.
verses.after: Do not offer the blood of my sacrifice with leavened bread, and do not leave the Passover festival sacrifice until morning.
verses.tsw_comparator: You shall not offer the blood of my sacrifice with anything leavened, and the sacrifice of the Passover festival shall not remain until morning.

verses.rationale: Retains clear wording shared with revised 23:19 because exact repeated firstfruits and cooking laws aid recognition, not novelty for its own sake.
verses.before: The best of the firstfruits of your ground you will bring to the house of the LORD your God. You will not boil a young goat in its mother’s milk.”
verses.after: Bring the first of your land’s firstfruits to the house of the LORD your God. Do not boil a young goat in its mother’s milk.”
verses.tsw_comparator: The best of the firstfruits of your ground you shall bring to the house of the LORD your God. You shall not boil a young goat in its mother’s milk.”

verses.rationale: Keeps write command, repeated words and both covenant partners without confusing with next verse’s unspecified writing subject.
verses.before: The LORD said to Moses, “Write these words, for according to these words I have made a covenant with you and with Israel.”
verses.after: The LORD told Moses, “Write down these words, for on the basis of these words I have made a covenant with you and with Israel.”
verses.tsw_comparator: The LORD said to Moses, “Write these words, for according to these words I have made a covenant with you and with Israel.”

verses.rationale: Retains duration, complete abstention and ambiguous he wrote rather than silently naming writer; uses literal Ten Words with familiar-title note.
verses.before: He was there with the LORD forty days and forty nights. He ate no bread and drank no water. And he wrote on the tablets the words of the covenant, the Ten Words.
verses.after: Moses was there with the LORD for forty days and forty nights. He ate no bread and drank no water. And he wrote on the tablets the words of the covenant, the Ten Words.
verses.tsw_comparator: He was there with the LORD forty days and forty nights. He ate no bread and drank no water. And he wrote on the tablets the words of the covenant, the Ten Words.

verses.rationale: Retains unawareness, two tablets, actual skin and radiance; names the LORD as conversation partner and notes that the Hebrew can also describe God speaking with Moses.
verses.before: When Moses came down from Mount Sinai with the two tablets of the testimony in Moses’ hand as he came down from the mountain, Moses did not know that the skin of his face was shining because he had spoken with him.
verses.after: When Moses came down Mount Sinai with the two tablets of the testimony in his hand, he did not know that the skin of his face shone because he had spoken with the LORD.
verses.tsw_comparator: When Moses came down from Mount Sinai with the two tablets of the testimony in Moses’ hand as he came down from the mountain, Moses did not know that the skin of his face was shining because he had spoken with him.

verses.rationale: Preserves named and collective observers, visible skin radiance and fear-driven distance.
verses.before: Aaron and all the children of Israel saw Moses, and look, the skin of his face was shining, and they were afraid to come near him.
verses.after: Aaron and all the Israelites saw Moses, and the skin of his face was shining. They were afraid to come near him.
verses.tsw_comparator: Aaron and all the children of Israel saw Moses, and look, the skin of his face was shining, and they were afraid to come near him.

verses.rationale: Keeps leaders’ return before all Israel approaches and explicitly identifies speaker.
verses.before: Moses called to them, and Aaron and all the leaders of the congregation returned to him, and Moses spoke with them.
verses.after: But Moses called to them. Aaron and all the community’s leaders came back to him, and Moses spoke with them.
verses.tsw_comparator: Moses called to them, and Aaron and all the leaders of the congregation returned to him, and Moses spoke with them.

verses.rationale: Preserves after sequence, comprehensive commands and named place of divine speech.
verses.before: Afterward all the children of Israel came near, and he commanded them all that the LORD had spoken with him on Mount Sinai.
verses.after: Afterward all the Israelites came near, and he gave them every command the LORD had spoken to him on Mount Sinai.
verses.tsw_comparator: Afterward all the children of Israel came near, and he commanded them all that the LORD had spoken with him on Mount Sinai.

verses.rationale: Preserves covering after public speech, not before, essential to following recurring veil sequence.
verses.before: When Moses finished speaking with them, he put a veil over his face.
verses.after: When Moses finished speaking with them, he put a veil over his face.
verses.tsw_comparator: When Moses finished speaking with them, he put a veil over his face.

verses.rationale: Keeps habitual entry/unveiling/exit/report sequence and passive commission without adding reason for veil.
verses.before: But whenever Moses went in before the LORD to speak with him, he removed the veil until he came out. Then he came out and spoke to the children of Israel what he had been commanded.
verses.after: Whenever Moses went in before the LORD to speak with him, he would take off the veil until he came out. Then he would come out and tell the Israelites what he had been commanded.
verses.tsw_comparator: But whenever Moses went in before the LORD to speak with him, he removed the veil until he came out. Then he came out and spoke to the children of Israel what he had been commanded.

verses.rationale: Preserves people actually seeing radiance before re-covering and next divine meeting; no added fading-glory explanation.
verses.before: The children of Israel saw the face of Moses, that the skin of Moses’ face was shining. Then Moses put the veil back over his face until he went in to speak with him.
verses.after: The Israelites would see Moses’ face, its skin shining. Then Moses would put the veil back over his face until he went in to speak with the LORD again.
verses.tsw_comparator: The children of Israel saw the face of Moses, that the skin of Moses’ face was shining. Then Moses put the veil back over his face until he went in to speak with him.
